newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan emperor ends self-imposed foreign travel ban.
newsitem.headline: Japan emperor ends self-imposed foreign travel ban.

text.p: Japanese Emperor Akihito said on Friday he abstained from overseas travel for the past two years to honour World War Two dead and the victims of the Kobe earthquake in 1995.
"I had a heavy heart these past two years," said Akihito, who appeared before the media with his wife Michiko in their first joint news conference in nearly three years.
"It was His Highness's heartfelt wish," Michiko said of the self-imposed moratorium on travel to mark the 50th anniversary of the war's end and the 1995 earthquake in which 6,000 people died.

The news conference was held ahead of the couple's two-week visit to Brazil, Argentina and Luxembourg from May 30. The last overseas trip by Akihito and Michiko was to France and Spain in October of 1994.

The trip also comes on the heels of the dramatic end to the Japan's four-month Peru hostage crisis, which began when Marxist rebels raided a party at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima to mark Akihito's birthday.

"I am very sorry that the chief judge of Peru and two Peruvians were killed," Akihito said. One hostage and two Peruvian commandos died in the dramatic rescue of hostages in the residence on April 22.
"I was deeply troubled that people were taken hostage at a reception for my birthday...I am very grateful for the efforts of all to resolve the incident," he said.
The trip to Latin America, which was postponed due to the hostage crisis, will be the first for a Japanese emperor.
When asked about criticism that the imperial household does not expose itself enough to the public, Michiko argued that there were ample opportunities to mingle with the people.
The empress said she left the palace on 12 occasions this past month, a relatively busy schedule for her, and said a large part of the couple's time was spent receiving people.
"I believe these duties (inside the palace) also play an important role of the imperial household, which is to appreciate the past and pass it on for a better future," Michiko said.
Akihito said he will ask the Household Agency to consider any concrete suggestions that will allow him to mingle more with the general public.
The couple is scheduled to arrive at the northern Brazilian city of Belem on May 31 via Luxembourg, and move on to Argentina from June 9 before returning to Tokyo.
During their stay, the royal couple will meet leaders of the two countries as well as Japanese immigrants and their descendants.
